Diagnostic Description
• Be sure to perform the Diagnostic

DTC Description
DTC U140087 Message of frame
$1E9 such as working status of vehicle
chassis system and status of vehicle are
lost
DTC U140287 Message of frame
$17D such as Antilock Brake System
Indication On are lost
DTC U140387 Message of frame $348
such as left and right Driven Wheel
Ground Velocity from ABS are lost
DTC U140487 Message of frame
$34A such as left and right Non Driven
Wheel Ground Velocity from ABS are
lost
DTC U140687 Message of frame $230
such as EPB working status from ESP
are lost
DTC U140787 Message of frame $128
such as Enhancement Longitudinal
Acceleration and ESP Master Cylinder
Brake Pressure from ESP are lost
DTC U140A87 Frame $0C1 refer to
left/right driven wheel distance pulse
counter and direction are lost
DTC U140B87 Frame $0C5 refer to
left/right Nondriven wheel distance pulse
counter and direction are lost
System Description
, Driving Assist Front Camera Assembly
through CAN Bus and ESC
communicate.
DTC Operating Conditions
• The detection starts after 1000ms
when the hard wire is in ON mode,
and stops when the hard wire is in
OFF mode.
DTC Setting Conditions
• DTC U140087 , U140387 ,
U140487 , U140787 , U140A87 ,
U140B87 ECU can’t detect this
message for consecutive 250 ms.
• DTC U140287 , U140687 ECU
can’t detect this message for 10
consecutive message periods.
Strategy after DTC Appears
• Record DTC, ACC unavailable, TJA
unavailable, AEB unavailable.
Clear Fault Information Conditions
• After 40 times no DTC circulation
( IGN ON to OFF ) , historic DTC
shall be cleared.
• Order for clearing DTC received
from Diag tools.

Circuit/System Inspection
1. Clear the malfunction codes and
check if the malfunction codes do
not reoccur?
Yes. Refer to the Testing for
intermittent conditions and poor
connections for intermittent
malfunctions.
No. Proceed to the next
inspection.
2. Check if other DTCs are set for the
system?
Yes. Perform the corresponding
malfunction diagnosis according
to the malfunction codes.
No. Proceed to the next
inspection.
3. Inspect the wiring harness
connectors for broken, poor contact,
aging and looseness?
Yes. Inspect and repair the
relevant malfunctions.
No. Proceed to the
"Circuit/System Testing".
Circuit/System Testing
Use the schematic to identify the
following
• Control module and local Internet
device equipped on the vehicle.
• Control module position on the high-
speed CAN serial data circuit.
• Control modules the vehicle is
equipped with Control module
locations on the low speed and
high-speed GMLAN serial data
circuits Control module B+, ignition,
ground, communication enable, and
serial data circuit terminals.
1. Confirm that there is no DTC
between other modules before
diagnosis. If there is a DTC,
diagnose it first.
2. Turn the ignition switch to position
"LOCK" and disconnect the battery
negative.
3. According to the conditions below,
test the resistance between terminal
6 (CAN-H) and 16 (CAN-L) of the
K56 Serial Data Gateway Module.
• Measure whether the
resistance is 60±5Ω when all
the connectors are connected.
• Measure whether the
resistance is 120±5Ω when the
connector in the Inflatable
Restraint Sensing and
Diagnostic Module or the Serial
Data Gateway Module is
separated.
• Measure whether the
resistance is infinite when the
connectors in the Inflatable
Restraint Sensing and
Diagnostic Module or the Serial
Data Gateway Module are
separated.
4. If the resistances above can’t meet
the standard value, the wiring
harness connector on the control
module that cannot communicate
needs to be disconnected.
5. Disconnect the K102 Vehicle
Stability Control Module wiring
harness connector. Disconnect the
QWL62 Driving Assist Front Camera
Assembly wiring harness connector.
6. C-CAN network H circuit check. Test
whether the resistance between
terminal 2 of the QWL62 Driving
Assist Front Camera Assembly
wiring harness connector and
terminal 5 of the K102 Vehicle
Stability Control Module wiring
harness connector is less than 1Ω?
No. Open circuit/resistance too
high fault.
Yes. Proceed the next diagnosis
step.
7. Test whether the resistance between
terminal 5 of the K102 Vehicle
Stability Control Module wiring
harness connector and ground are
infinite?
No. Short circuit to ground.
Yes. Proceed the next diagnosis
step.
8. Connect the battery negative and
turn the ignition switch to position
"ON".
9. Test whether the voltage between
terminal 5 of the K102 Vehicle
Stability Control Module wiring
harness connector and ground is 2.7
± 0.1V?
No. Short circuit to power.
Yes. Proceed the next diagnosis
step.
10. Turn the ignition switch to position
"LOCK" and disconnect the battery
negative.
11. C-CAN network L circuit check. Test
whether the resistance between
terminal 3 of the QWL62 Driving
Assist Front Camera Assembly
wiring harness connector and
terminal 19 of the K102 Vehicle
Stability Control Module wiring
harness connector is less than 1Ω?
No. Open circuit/resistance too
high fault.
Yes. Proceed the next diagnosis
step.
12. Test whether the resistance between
terminal 19 of the K102 Vehicle
Stability Control Module wiring
harness connector and ground are
infinite?
No. Short circuit to ground.
Yes. Proceed the next diagnosis
step.
13. Connect the battery negative and
turn the ignition switch to position
"ON".
14. Test whether the voltage between
terminal 19 of the K102 Vehicle
Stability Control Module wiring
harness connector and ground is
2.3±0.1V?
No. Short circuit to power.
Yes. Proceed the next diagnosis
step.
15. Turn the ignition switch to position
"LOCK" and disconnect the battery
negative.
16. Replace the Vehicle Stability Control
Module or the Driving Assist Front
Camera Assembly. Operate the
vehicle in the DTC operating
conditions. Whether the DTC is set?
No. Diagnosis completed.
Yes. Install the original module
and contact the technical
engineer.
